subject: mechanical
audience: FE Mechanical candidates and mechanical engineering students
title: The Pump That Needed 14 kW to Deliver 9.81 kW to the Water
featured_title: THE PUMP THAT NEEDED 14 KW TO DELIVER 9.81 KW TO THE WATER

presentation.challenge: The water received 9.81 kW. A 70% efficient pump required about 14.0 kW of shaft input.

practice.primary_question: Why is pump shaft input power larger than hydraulic power delivered to the fluid?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Multiplying hydraulic power by efficiency when solving for required pump input power instead of dividing by efficiency.

case_dna.target_misconception: If a pump is 70% efficient, its required shaft input is hydraulic power multiplied by 0.70.
case_dna.why_plausible: Efficiency is often described as '70% of the input becomes useful output,' and the direction of the ratio can be reversed accidentally.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: Hydraulic power is ρgQH=1000×9.81×0.05×20=9.81 kW. With η=P_hyd/P_in=0.70, input power is 9.81/0.70≈14.0 kW.
case_dna.corrected_model: Pump efficiency is useful hydraulic output divided by shaft input, so required input is P_hyd/η.

problem_statement: A pump moves water at 0.050 m³/s against a 20 m head. Water density is 1000 kg/m³ and pump efficiency is 70%. A sizing note multiplies hydraulic power by 0.70 and specifies a motor smaller than the useful fluid power. Determine hydraulic power and required shaft input.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The motor was sized below the useful water power.
gates.prompt: Which power belongs in the numerator of pump efficiency?
gates.cta: Separate hydraulic output from shaft input

options.label: Compute P_hyd=ρgQH, then P_in=P_hyd/η
options.reason: Pump efficiency is useful hydraulic output divided by shaft input.

options.label: Compute P_in=P_hyd×η
options.reason: That would make input smaller than useful output for an efficiency below 100%.

options.label: Pump power depends only on head, not flow rate
options.reason: Hydraulic power depends on both Q and H.

gates.label: Predict
gates.heading: Predict the required shaft power
gates.prompt: What shaft input power in kW is required?

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Load the pump
gates.result: The required shaft input is about 14.0 kW.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove hydraulic and input power
gates.success: Hydraulic power is 9.81 kW; shaft input is 9.81/0.70≈14.01 kW.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: The efficiency ratio sets the direction of the calculation

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the motor-sizing note
report: C3. Required shaft input is 9.81×0.70=6.87 kW.

claims.label: C1
claims.reason: The useful fluid power is correct.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: It reverses the efficiency relationship and predicts input below useful output.

evidence_choices.label: P_in=P_hyd/η=9.81/0.70≈14.01 kW
evidence_choices.reason: This correctly interprets efficiency as output divided by input.

correction.template: The pump requires about {input} kW of shaft input for the stated duty.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Reduce required shaft input without changing Q or H
gates.constraint: Keep the same flow rate and head.

options.label: Use a higher-efficiency pump
options.reason: For fixed hydraulic power, P_in=P_hyd/η decreases as η increases.

options.label: Use a lower-efficiency pump
options.reason: That increases the required shaft power.

options.label: Size the motor only to 9.81 kW
options.reason: That leaves no allowance for pump inefficiency in this idealized sizing calculation.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply pump efficiency
gates.prompt: A pump delivers 12 kW of hydraulic power at 80% efficiency. What shaft input is required?

options.label: 9.6 kW
options.reason: That multiplies by efficiency in the wrong direction.

gates.explanation: Required input equals useful hydraulic output divided by efficiency.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the pump-power model
gates.confirmation: I confirm that pump efficiency is hydraulic output divided by shaft input, so input power exceeds useful fluid power when efficiency is below 100%.

items.label: What failed
items.value: Efficiency was applied in the wrong direction.

items.label: What was assumed
items.value: Input power was taken as hydraulic power times efficiency.

seo.seo_title: Pump Power and Efficiency: Why 9.81 kW Needs 14 kW Input | FE E-056
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Mechanical Case E-056: a water pump delivering 9.81 kW hydraulically at 70% efficiency requires about 14.0 kW shaft input.
seo.excerpt: Useful hydraulic power is not the same as motor or shaft input. Efficiency determines how much extra input is required.
seo.direct_answer: Hydraulic pump power is ρgQH. For water at Q=0.05 m³/s and H=20 m, P_hyd=9.81 kW. At 70% efficiency, required shaft input is 9.81/0.70≈14.0 kW.

faqs.q: How do you calculate hydraulic pump power?
Why divide by efficiency for pump input power?
faqs.a: Because pump efficiency equals useful hydraulic output divided by shaft input.
